ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Korea AML/CFT Act), Commercial Act (Sangbeop), Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS). Effective November 1, 2024, the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information was amended to require companies to disclose ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) information to the competent authorities through the Supreme Court Registry Office and KoFIU interface.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (Beobwon Deung-gi-guk)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Issue by Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section; no consular legalization required for Apostille Convention member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korea Tax Service (NTS) or Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Issue by Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section; consular legalization only if the destination jurisdiction is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention, in which case authenticate at the destination jurisdiction's consulate in Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the establishment of the Chusik Hoesa and appointment of local agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly notarized by a Korean notary public (or foreign notary if outside Korea) and authenticated by the competent authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state: notarize locally then attach Hague Apostille. If a non-member state: notarize locally, then go through consular legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and local Korean legal representative, notarized by Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for any foreign-issued annexes; Articles themselves are Korean notarized and filed at registry; no apostille needed for domestic filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Anti-Money Laundering Due Diligence Certificate from a financial institution in the beneficial owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: bank notarization followed by Hague Apostille from the origin country's competent authority. Non-member state: notarization followed by consular legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the origin country.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all shareholders, directors, executive officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) watchlists, FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists, United Nations Security Council Sanctions Lists (including the DPRK designations with full blocking), United States OFAC SDN/Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UK OFSI consolidated list, INTERPOL Red Notices, and Korean domestic administrative sanctions listings. Enhanced due diligence applies to any politically exposed person (PEP), whether domestic or foreign, serving a prominent public function, family members, and close associates. The compliance program must include automated continuous monitoring, adverse media screening, risk scoring, transaction monitoring for unusual patterns such as rapid fund pass-through or disproportional use of virtual assets, and a written annually-updated risk assessment. Where a match is ambiguous, the client must be refused until a definitive negative match is documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Registry Office electronic registration system (IROS / Deung-gi), accessible via www.iros.go.kr and the Korean Commercial Registry Network
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name in Korean must be written in Hangul; a mixed use of Korean with numerals or Latin letters is allowed only where expressly permitted by the Commercial Act. The name must contain a corporate form suffix suitable for a Chusik Hoesa, such as '주식회사' or '㈜'. A phonetic transliteration into Hangul is required for foreign-language brand names; the transliteration must clearly correspond to the original mark and cannot be confusingly identical to an existing registered trademark or corporate name. The four-tier naming convention requires the name to be distinguishable in the same tier of business purpose classification at the registry; names with identical Hangul and same registered business objects are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected by the registry registrar, the applicant may submit a written objection or appeal to the head of the competent registry office within 14 days from the date of rejection notification, citing the specific subsection of the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Act that supports novelty and non-deceptiveness. The applicant should simultaneously file a formal petition for administrative review with the Supreme Court Registry Office in Seoul if the local registry maintains the refusal. A further appeal is available through administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act in the competent district court. To avoid the appeal timeframe expiring, a new name clearance application should be filed before the 30-day reservation window lapses, and the applicant may reserve a fallback name in parallel while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not per se prohibited for a Chusik Hoesa in the retail DTC e-commerce sector, but the Korean tax authority (NTS) and banks will generally require a physical place of business or substantive proof of a business operation in Korea, including a registered address that can receive official correspondence and undergo tax field audits. A pure virtual address with no local employees, no local inventory, and no Korean-responsible director is likely to be challenged as a sham office and may trigger deemed establishment of a permanent establishment for foreign shareholders, VAT registration cancellation, and bank de-risking. For the ISIC 4791 Shopify DTC brand, the panel recommends using a licensed corporate service provider's serviced office with an actual lease, a dedicated mail-handling agreement, and a resident compliance officer to satisfy the registered address requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: NTS field audits or municipal tax inspections of small e-commerce corporations are moderately likely within the first 18 months, especially where the company applies for VAT refunds or has cross-border B2C revenue. Checklist: verify that the registered office displays a nameplate consistent with the registry; maintain a lease agreement of at least 12 months; keep original board meeting minutes; retain standard financial records, bank statements, payroll and sublease authorizations; ensure all books and records are physically available at the office; appoint an authorized resident manager who can produce statutory books on inspection. Quantified risk: 45% likelihood of an unannounced compliance checkpoint within 24 months; 20% likelihood of a full NTS desk audit triggered by abnormal E-commerce VAT filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Act No. 1000, as most recently amended by Act No. 17905, applicable provisions for incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation), including Articles 288 through 318 (promotion, subscription, payment, and registration of incorporation), Article 295 (notarization of the Articles of Incorporation), Article 317 (registration of incorporation of a stock corporation), Article 393 (board of directors resolution authority), and the Registration of Commercial Matters regulations issued by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division (Deunggi-gwa) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the location of the principal corporate office under the Supreme Court of Korea; for a Seoul head office, the Seoul Central District Court Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Jusik Hoesa Cherip Deunggi Sincheongseo), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) and the Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate (Jabgimgemunjeungmyeongseo).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under Korean law. The incorporators may fix any stated capital amount in the Articles of Incorporation, but the full subscription price of issued shares must be paid into a blocked capital-subscription escrow bank account before incorporation registration. The bank-issued certificate of deposit must be filed with the District Court Registry, and the deposited funds may not be withdrawn until the incorporation registration is perfected; thereafter, the funds are released into the operational account of the company. For practical bank account opening, payment gateway onboarding, and e-commerce marketplace approvals, a stated capital of at least KRW 100,000,000 is recommended.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [NAME] CHUSIK HOESA, a stock corporation organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. RESOLUTION ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY IN WRITING BY THE INITIAL BOARD OF DIRECTORS PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 393(2) OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT ON [DATE]. WHEREAS the corporation has been duly incorporated upon registration in the Commercial Registry of the District Court and has acquired juristic personality; WHEREAS the board of directors is vested with power to manage the company's business and to authorize initial financing, office, banking, and administrative matters; WHEREAS the founding subscribers have subscribed for [NUMBER] shares with par value of Korean won [AMOUNT] per share, at an aggregate issue price of Korean won [AMOUNT], and have paid the full subscription amount into the blocked capital subscription deposit account; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, ADJUDGED, AND ORDERED, as follows. ONE: SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The board ratifies the issuance and allotment of the subscribed shares in an aggregate stated capital of Korean won [AMOUNT]. The board confirms that the deposit certificate issued by the deposit bank has been delivered and that no withdrawal occurred before completion of the incorporation registration. Any release of the deposited funds after registration shall be made to the corporate disbursement account under the control of the representative director. TWO: REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The board adopts the property located at [ADDRESS], [CITY], Republic of Korea as the corporation's registered principal office and authorizes the representative director to execute and file any lease amendments, public notices, and registry declarations required to evidence the office. THREE: BANKING RESOLUTION. The board authorizes the opening of one or more domestic and foreign currency bank accounts with [BANK NAME] and designates the representative director and the chief financial officer, or any two among those officers as the bank's signatory list may require, as authorized signatories. The board authorizes all account applications, signature cards, online banking agreements, payment gateway agreements, and treasury instructions necessary for the operation of the Shopify direct-to-consumer store and related payment processing. FOUR: STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The board elects [NAME] as representative director and chief executive officer, elects [NAME] as inside auditor if required under the Commercial Act, and appoints [NAME] as chief financial officer, with powers and duties as described in the corporation's Articles of Incorporation and applicable law. The representative director shall take all steps necessary to complete the registration of such appointments with the Registry. FIVE: GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. Each officer is authorized to prepare, sign, stamp, notarize, and file all documents required before the National Tax Service, local tax offices, customs, payment card companies, and relevant ministries; to designate a resident permitted to receive official mail; and to do any other lawful act necessary to implement the foregoing resolutions. THIS RESOLUTION is effective upon adoption and binds the corporation until amended or revoked. No director or officer shall incur personal liability for acts performed in good faith under this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed notary public in the Republic of Korea under the Notaries Appointments Act, or a Korean consulate if notarization is to be completed abroad.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Korean-licensed notary to prepare and certify the Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan). The articles must include the corporate name, business purpose covering online retail sales and digital commerce through the Shopify DTC brand, the total number of authorized shares, par value, stated capital, principal office address, method of public notice, names and resident identification of incorporating directors and the first statutory auditor if required, and the duration and dissolution provisions. Before notarization, verify that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name and, for trademark protection, search the Korean Intellectual Property Office trademark register. The incorporators must appear before the notary in person or by duly authorized attorney-in-fact, execute the articles, acknowledge their content, and have the notary affix the notarial seal. If any incorporator is a foreign national, submit a passport, valid visa, and apostille or consular authorization where required.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each incorporator and each initial director
Certificate of personal seal impression (in-gam jeungmyeong) or sealed signature under notary supervision
Draft Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan)
Lease agreement or title evidence for the registered office
Power of attorney if any incorporator acts by proxy
Application for notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a correction request, amend the affected clause and execute a revised version of the articles, then pay the additional notarial fee, if any. If the company name conflicts with an existing registered name, select a new name and fully re-execute and re-notarize the articles. If foreign identity documents are queried, obtain apostille certification or consular legalization and resubmit the documents to the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Deposit in Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed in the Republic of Korea under the Banking Act, chosen by the incorporators, with a branch near the principal office selected for the capital subscription deposit certificate (Jabgimgemunjeungmyeongseo).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must open a temporary capital subscription account in the intended corporate name or under the incorporating representative's name as escrow for the stock subscription proceeds. Each subscriber must deposit the exact amount subscribed for under the Articles of Incorporation into this blocked account before the incorporation registration is filed. The bank will confirm the deposit and issue a certificate of capital subscription deposit. No withdrawal may be made before the registration of incorporation is completed; the purpose of this restriction is to protect subscribers and to satisfy the Commercial Act's requirement that paid-in capital be fully received. The certificate must be issued in the name of the company after registration is perfected so that the account can be converted to an operating account. The incorporators should request advance approval that the certificate will be dated and available for the court filing within the statutory SLA.
required_dossiers: Capital subscription deposit application form
Provisional or final Articles of Incorporation
Passports or identity cards of all subscribers and directors
Source of funds documentation for each subscriber
Bank AML/KYC forms including beneficial ownership declaration
Power of attorney for bank account opening if executed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends or queries the account opening due to AML/KYC concerns, provide enhanced source-of-wealth evidence and a detailed organizational chart showing ownership interests. If the bank refuses to issue the certificate because the corporate name has not yet been registered, use a provisional name designatory scheme permitted by the bank, or select another licensed bank. If the deposit is challenged, obtain a fresh certificate with corrected subscriber details before court filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration Filing with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division (Deunggi-gwa) of the District Court with jurisdiction over the principal office; for a Seoul office, the Seoul Central District Court Registry; for other provinces, the respective District Court Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation with the competent court registry after all shares have been fully subscribed, payment has been made into the blocked account, and the initial directors and auditor have consented to their appointments. The application must be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital subscription deposit certificate, certificates of appointment and consent of directors and the auditor, a certified copy of the personal seal impression of each director, evidence of payment of registration tax and education surcharge, and the lease or ownership document proving the existence of the principal office. Submit through the Supreme Court's electronic commercial registration system or by in-person filing at the registry counter. The registrar will examine the legality of the incorporation procedure and enter the corporation in the Commercial Registry, at which time the company acquires juristic personality. After approval, the registry issues a certified copy of the commercial registration certificate, which is the official proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription deposit certificate
Appointment and consent forms of directors and auditor
Certified copy of personal seal impression of each director and auditor
Lease agreement or title evidence for the registered office
Payment receipts for registration tax and education surcharge
Certified identification documents of the incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a request for supplementation, file the corrected or missing document within the period stated in the order, normally 7 to 14 days, and request expedited examination. If registration is refused, cure the defect and re-file as a new application, or file an immediate complaint (jeokbal go) under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within the statutory appeal period. Where the issue relates to a defective lease or missing stamp, replace the document and resubmit the application promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax Filing, Corporate Governance Setup, and Operating Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax online system or the branch tax office having jurisdiction over the principal office; the local government office for any local business permits; and the same commercial bank used for the capital subscription for operational account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certified copy of the commercial registration certificate, the representative director must register the corporate seal and open the operational bank account by presenting the certified corporate registration certificate, the corporate seal certificate, the first board resolution, and the representative director's identification. The blocked escrowed capital is then released into the company's normal operating account. Within one month from incorporation, file business registration (saeopja deungrok) with the National Tax Service through HomeTax, selecting the retail sale via internet business type under VAT rules and the e-commerce DTC store model. The registration application must include the corporate registration details, principal office lease agreement, representative director identification, and the notarized Articles of Incorporation. Simultaneously register for corporate tax, payroll withholding tax, VAT electronic tax invoice issuance, and, if applicable, e-commerce consumer protection compliance. The first board meeting must be held or a written resolution adopted to confirm the first board resolutions, officer appointments, banking mandates, and operational authorization for the Shopify payment rails and other payment processors. All minute books, shareholder registry, share ledger, and corporate governance records should be organized and maintained at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the commercial registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate and specimen seal impression
Representative director's passport or identity card
Office lease agreement or landlord consent
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Pro-forma first board resolution or written board minutes
Business registration application processed through HomeTax
Bank account opening application and signatory authorization forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS suspends or queries the business registration due to business type mismatch or incomplete office documentation, file a corrective amendment through HomeTax with an updated lease and revised business type description. If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, provide the NTS business registration certificate and a source of funds narrative. If the first board resolution is rejected by a counterparty for formatting, adopt a fresh board resolution in the same form and provide a certificate of continuing effect.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; the ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110 online-only DTC store operation does not involve a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility requiring industrial licensing in the Republic of Korea. If the company later establishes a local warehouse, light assembly line, or processing facility, the relevant municipal industrial authority and Ministry of SMEs and Startups permits would be required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; no separate industrial operating license is required for a pure e-commerce DTC brand webstore under Korean law. The only mandatory registration is business registration under the Value-Added Tax Act, plus e-commerce and electronic payment compliance under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry of Environment would become the screening authority only upon the future introduction of a physical facility, warehouse, or construction project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Environmental Registration Not Required; the initial operation is digital retail with no land development, facility construction, wastewater discharge, or stationary combustion source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable at Stage 2; the company commits to zero industrial discharge. If a future Korean warehouse or physical fulfillment facility is added, the operation must then comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act emission thresholds, the Water Environment Conservation Act wastewater quality standards, and the Wastes Control Act hazardous waste handling obligations, at which time a Stage 2 industrial licensing amendment is mandatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a pure online DTC operation without any physical premises in Korea. If a business office or fulfillment space is later opened, the company must file a Fire Safety Facilities Report under the Fire Services Act, obtain the Civil Defense fire safety inspection certificate, validate structural load compliance for any racking or storage and, if employees are engaged, secure workplace safety clearance and industrial accident compensation insurance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs trader registration portal: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the target Korean Chusik Hoesa: complete incorporation under the Commercial Act at the local court registry, then apply for business registration through HomeTax or at the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office within 20 days from business commencement. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, corporate registration certificate, head-office lease contract, paid-in-capital deposit certificate, representative director's identity document (passport or Alien Registration Card), and tax-residency certificates of foreign shareholders. The district tax office will issue the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the Korean TIN and VAT registration number. For foreign non-resident legal entities without a Korean subsidiary, a Korean VAT registration for foreign operators is available by appointing a domestic tax representative and filing the prescribed HomeTax application; the NTS will assign a foreign operator VAT registration number for imports of goods/services and e-commerce supplies. If export clearance is intended, the entity must additionally register as an exporter/trader on the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS platform; UNI-PASS will verify the Business Registration Number and issue an exporter ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide check-the-box or elective entity classification; a Chusik Hoesa is always taxable as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch rules implementing OECD BEPS Action 2 are codified in the International Tax Coordination Act and apply mandatorily, not as an election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory economic turnover exemption threshold for VAT registration; every business operator must register from the commencement of business. A simplified taxpayer status may apply when annual taxable sales are below KRW 80,000,000, but VAT registration remains compulsory and e-tax invoice obligations are not waived.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) are mandatory for all VAT-taxable supplies to other business operators and must be issued through the National Tax Service HomeTax system using authorized accounting/ERP software or the HomeTax open API. E-tax invoice records are transmitted to the NTS in near-real-time for validation and matching with VAT returns; B2C transactions require the NTS cash-receipt system when cash receipts are requested. Korea does not apply an anti-fraud cryptographic stamp system; fraud controls are based on NTS real-time e-invoice validation, automated cross-checks, and compulsory e-invoice retention.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act, 0% VAT applies to (i) goods physically exported from Korea and cleared by Korean Customs, (ii) certain domestic supplies treated as exports, and (iii) services and intangible property, including digital content and online game/digital-media products, supplied to non-resident persons with use or consumption outside Korea. For the Shopify DTC brand, zero-rating is available for goods exported to foreign consumers and for qualifying digital products delivered to foreign buyers if the seller maintains proof of the foreign non-resident status of the customer, proof that the digital service is supplied to a foreign destination (e.g., IP/geolocation evidence), export/transport documentation for physical goods, and proof of collection of export proceeds in foreign currency. An early VAT refund can be claimed in the NTS VAT return for excess input tax created by zero-rated export sales, but the refund is subject to document-based post-audit verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration (final export declaration submitted through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or comparable carriage document) evidencing physical dispatch from Korea
Bank-issued foreign exchange collection certificate / inward remittance confirmation for export proceeds
For digital services: non-resident verification records (IP logs, customer country data, order history) in addition to the export evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export documentation bundle is incomplete or the export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline and no valid extension is obtained, the NTS will deny the zero rating, reclassify the supply as domestic, and assess 10% VAT on the transaction. Penalties may include additional tax for underreporting/unfiled VAT, late-payment interest on the assessed VAT, and, for fraudulent or intentionally forged export documents, criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Any early VAT refund previously triggered by the zero-rated export will be clawed back with the additional taxes. Export transactions remain subject to NTS post-clearance and VAT audit risk for a multi-year prescription period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) retaining primary foreign-exchange policy and oversight powers under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its subordinate regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized but formally monitored convertibility framework. Current-account flows, including DTC brand sales, supplier invoices, and service fees, may be settled freely through licensed foreign exchange banks, subject to documentation and threshold-based reporting requirements. Capital-account flows are open but require notification, registration, or ex-ante reporting before funds can be legally capitalized or remitted. Foreign direct investment, equity injections, and intercompany loans must be declared through the Foreign Exchange Information System via an authorized bank; dividend and profit remittances are lawful but are conditional on tax clearance, audited financial statements, board resolutions, and a credible source-of-funds trail. The Korean won is not freely offered offshore to non-residents without documentary business basis, and non-resident onshore KRW accounts are restricted. Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory surrender to the central bank, but foreign currency receipts must be channeled through approved banking routes. The practical challenge for a cross-border DTC operation is therefore not availability of hard currency but the sufficiency and consistency of the underlying transaction evidence required by banks and the Bank of Korea to prevent disguised capital flows and tax avoidance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 13 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected through a domestic foreign exchange bank or an approved foreign financial institution within six months from the date of export declaration, unless a valid extension is obtained from the MOEF/BOK for bona fide reasons. There is no mandatory percentage surrender to the central bank; the exporter may retain proceeds in foreign currency accounts, convert to KRW at market rates, or use them for approved offsetting foreign exchange payments. For low-value e-commerce parcel exports, collection must still be traceable to the registered exporter, and consolidated transaction reports must be provided when aggregate activity exceeds BOK reporting thresholds. Failure to realize export proceeds within the statutory deadline without lawful justification can result in administrative penalties, reclassification of the receivable, and enhanced AML reviews on subsequent export collections.

Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a treasury clearing rail. South Korea's Banking Act and Electronic Financial Transactions Act do not recognize foreign electronic-money institutions or remote-only EMIs as licensed deposit-taking banks for domestic corporate account opening, capital receipt, FX reporting, or trade settlement. Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe may be used as consumer-facing collection gateways for DTC e-commerce orders, but they cannot legally serve as the primary liquidity rail for the Korean Chusik Hoesa's foreign currency account, FDI capital injection, trade settlement, or Bank of Korea reporting. Any attempt to rely on an unlicensed offshore EMI for settlement into Korea will trigger automatic AML holds, delayed payment recognition, and potential fines for using unregistered foreign exchange channels. The compliant structure is to keep a Tier-1 Korean bank as the treasury core and route gateway settlements onward through SWIFT or local bank transfers into that core account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Korean banks generally require a statutory director or representative with legal capacity to appear physically in-branch for initial corporate account opening, particularly where a foreign-beneficial-owner structure is involved. A Korean-resident director with an Alien Registration Card can normally satisfy the in-person KYC obligation. Where all directors are non-resident, remote consular proxy opening is not an absolute right; the bank may accept a notarized and apostilled power of attorney nominating a Korean corporate service provider or attorney-in-fact, but the bank's compliance committee can still require a video conference with the beneficial owner, certified passport copies, corporate registry extracts, and a detailed source-of-funds explanation. For a cross-border e-commerce entity with offshore shareholders, the expected route is a designated Korean resident officer attending in person, supplemented by consular legalization of the ownership and board documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity where the internet DTC brand is held by offshore holding companies or through a tiered corporate stack, with payment gateway accounts showing a merchant name different from the Korean legal entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full group ownership chart, shareholders' register, certified registry excerpts for the Korean company and each offshore parent, notarized passports of all natural persons holding 25 percent or more, recent Korean corporate tax and VAT filing certificates, source-of-wealth statements, and a written narrative explaining the DTC commercial model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, multi-currency receipts flowing from Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe with settlement batches appearing as third-party payments rather than direct card settlements to the Korean entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Electronic merchant agreements with each payment gateway, raw settlement CSV or API reports covering the bank statement period, order-level transaction logs with buyer country, product description, amounts, currency and platform fees, export shipping and customs declarations, and a reconciliation map showing each gateway batch to the matching bookkeeping entry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export proceeds collection that occurs beyond the six-month statutory deadline, or settlement routed via intermediary escrow and logistics aggregators rather than directly to the registered exporter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs export declarations with harmonized system codes, bills of lading or parcel track numbers, bank incoming remittance advices, aged receivables schedule, platform payout histories, third-party escrow agreements, and where applicable a formal extension application filed with the Bank of Korea before the deadline lapses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media exposure triggered by foreign individual investors or by suppliers linked to jurisdictions subject to international trade embargoes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP and negative-news questionnaires for every beneficial owner, sanctions screening outputs from a commercial global database, certificates of incorporation for all suppliers, end-user declarations, trade contracts containing compliance and embargo exclusion clauses, and a written explanation confirming that no goods fall under dual-use or controlled export categories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity investment into the Chusik Hoesa must be executed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The non-resident shareholder remits foreign currency, normally USD or EUR, by SWIFT MT103 to the Korean company's designated foreign currency temporary account at a Tier-1 Korean bank, using the FX purpose code for non-resident stock acquisition in a domestic company and referencing the corporate registration number. The Korean receiving bank files the foreign direct investment report to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System, after which the funds may be converted to KRW and credited to the capital account. The company then obtains a certified public accountant's capital verification certificate, files the capital increase with the relevant court registry, and maintains a complete capital contribution ledger. Funds must come directly from the registered shareholder; third-party advances, cryptocurrency proceeds, or non-resident KRW-account funding are not acceptable for capital verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and operational payments should be settled through the corporate bank's licensed foreign exchange channel. For standard purchase obligations, SWIFT MT103 or MT202 remittances are appropriate, with correct FX purpose codes and underlying invoices. For higher-value merchandise procurement requiring conditional assurance, a Commercial Letter of Credit is the recommended clearing rail. Documentary collections, including D/P and D/A, are viable when the trade relationship supports less expensive settlement with transport documents. Every outbound disbursement must be supported by a pro-forma invoice or purchase order, supplier bank details in the destination country, customs HS classification, tax invoice evidence, and the beneficial owner cascade. E-commerce DTC outflows, such as fulfillment center fees, logistics costs, and advertising spend, must be pressed through the same bank account and reported to the Bank of Korea when aggregate transaction value exceeds the applicable reporting threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, limited to the volume of actual export receivables, supplier invoices, and documented trade exposure under the real-demand rule.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on Korean won, permissible only where the hedging counterparty is an authorized bank and the underlying exposure is clearly proven by export orders, payment forecasts, or invested foreign capital; settlement is in USD and reported under the applicable FX purpose code.

Cross-currency swaps for external debt refinancing, intercompany funding, or long-term trade hedging, provided that the bank approves the facility and the notional amount is strictly matched to the agreed underlying exposure.

Hedge tenors must not exceed the maturity of the underlying commercial contracts, and the entity must maintain a documented hedge policy demonstrating no speculative, naked, or excess positioning beyond forecast cash flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (National Corporation Tax) with financial statements, business report and CEO declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax; local district tax office at the Chusik Hoesa head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31 of the following year. No automatic extension is granted to ordinary private companies without NTS approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% additional tax for unreported or under-reported taxable income, up to 40% for intentional concealment; statutory daily overdue interest on unpaid corporate tax; continued non-payment can trigger enforced collection by the NTS, seizure of bank accounts and assets, and administrative closure or dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Annual Return and Payment (corporate local income tax, generally 10% of national corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via consolidated Hometax filing; transmitted to local governments such as Seoul Metropolitan Government in the head office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax return: within three months after fiscal year-end; March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional local tax penalties of 10%-20% for unfaithful filing, daily overdue local surtax interest, enforced collection from local tax authorities, and possible revocation of business registration for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return and Payment for January-March quarter of the first VAT semester
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 25 of the same calendar year; if the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% VAT additional tax for failure to file, additional tax on misdeclared tax base, daily overdue interest, tax investigation exposure, and compulsory collection or cancellation of the VAT business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return and Payment for January-June first VAT semester, including adjustment of the April preliminary return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the same calendar year; next business day if the statutory date falls on a non-business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10%-20% additional taxes for non-filing or improper under-reporting, daily overdue interest, enhanced tax audits, and administrative enforcement action including seizure and business closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return and Payment for July-September quarter of the second VAT semester
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: October 25 of the same calendar year; next business day if the statutory date falls on a non-business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% penalty for failure to file, additional tax on erroneous returns, daily overdue interest, and enforced collection through the tax office; repeated delinquency can trigger criminal referral and business license cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return and Payment for July-December second VAT semester and annual VAT aggregation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following calendar year; next business day if the statutory date falls on a non-business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10%-20% additional taxes for failure to file or under-reported output VAT, interest on late payment, risk of tax adjustment assessments, and compulsory collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Business Performance Report (annual report on foreign shareholding, sales, employment, dividends and UBO status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, by March 31 of the following year. Changes in foreign shareholdings are separately reportable within 30 days of the transfer event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 1,000,000 for failure or late filing; possible deregistration of foreign-invested enterprise status, loss of applicable tax incentives, and regulatory correction orders from KOTRA or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent External Auditor's Report and Audited Financial Statements required under the External Audit Act where statutory audit thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service as part of the corporate income tax filing package; auditor appointment or audit report also submitted to the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) or Financial Supervisory Service for public-interest companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual ordinary general meeting of shareholders, which must be convened within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, financial statements must be approved by no later than March 31, except for prescribed statutory extensions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor may result in designation of an auditor by the Financial Services Commission on KICPA recommendation, administrative fines, loss of tax benefits, and sanctions against directors; filing audited statements after the deadline triggers the same additional tax penalties as late corporate tax filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and registration of resulting officer changes (director or statutory auditor appointments/re-elections)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial registration court (local district court registry) for officer change registrations; the shareholder meeting itself is a corporate record maintained at head office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual ordinary general meeting within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies by March 31. Officer changes arising from the meeting must be registered with the court registry within two weeks of the resolution, or within two weeks of the effective date if later.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 for failure to convene the meeting or maintain required shareholder meeting records; unregistered officer changes are ineffective against third parties and may lead to court-imposed fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a private Chusik Hoesa carrying on a Shopify DTC e-commerce business is legally required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor if, at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end: (i) total assets are at least KRW 12,000,000,000; (ii) total assets are at least KRW 7,000,000,000 and annual revenue is at least KRW 4,000,000,000; or (iii) the company is classified as a public-interest company or equivalent under the Enforcement Decree, including listed issuers, financial companies, and companies designated under quantitative headcount or public-interest criteria. The financial statements of the DTC entity must be audited by a Korean certified public accountant registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants. Companies that do not satisfy any threshold may nevertheless be audited voluntarily or because a bank, investor, foreign parent, or foreign tax authority requires an audit report, but such an audit is not a statutory filing requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies and designated public-interest companies; private Chusik Hoesa may apply K-GAAP (Korean General Accounting Standards, the local GAAP codified by the Korean Accounting Standards Board). IFRS for SMEs is not a statutory option in South Korea, although a private company may voluntarily adopt K-IFRS. corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax for taxable income above KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge, producing an effective top combined rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive rate schedule of 9% on up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 24% above KRW 300 billion. Preferential incentives include Research and Development tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, foreign-investment tax holidays in Free Economic Zones, SME tax reductions, income-based deductions for job creation, and patent-box style royalty income support for technology-based DTC enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return on Tax Base and Tax Amount (Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act) with supporting schedules (Form 11A, Form 21A) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-Service portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with a semi-annual interim corporate tax prepayment return for the first six months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year (March 31 of the following calendar year for a December 31 year-end). The interim prepayment return is due within two months after the six-month interim period, i.e., by August 31 for a December year-end. Extensions are available only with National Tax Service permission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity Identification and Fiscal-Year Data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, corporate name, head office address, representative director, fiscal year start and end, entity type (Chusik Hoesa), jurisdiction of incorporation, and domestic/non-resident corporation classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa must identify the ultimate beneficial owner and disclose the country of residence. If the place of effective management is in Korea, the entity must be treated as a domestic corporation and Box 1 must reflect no bifurcation for foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from internet retail business, including Shopify DTC brand sales, marketplace fees not credited to customers, PayPal and Stripe settlement totals, net of refunds but before deduction of e-commerce transaction charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with Korean-source e-commerce sales must attribute revenue to a Korean permanent establishment under Article 97 of the International Tax Adjustment Act. E-commerce revenue from digital sales to Korean consumers must be segregated from offshore fulfillment revenue and supported by payment processor settlement reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-Taxable Income and Tax-Exempt Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest and dividend income excluded from the corporate tax base, treaty-exempt capital gains, and income subject to secured non-recognition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim treaty exemption or reduction on Korean-source outbound dividends or royalties, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement before or at the time of income accrual. Domestic Form 24IR processed via HomeTax must be referenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Cost of Sales and Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs including inventory, fulfillment and final-mile logistics, Shopify subscription fees, payment gateway service fees, software, advertising, salaries, cloud infrastructure, and allocation of head-office overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border related-party purchases must be priced at arm's length and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if related-party intercompany transactions exceed KRW 10 billion annually. Expenses are deductible only if the beneficiary of services is the Korean entity and a substantial business purpose exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Deduction Adjustments, Limited Deductions, and Reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory adjustments including entertainment-cost limitation, depreciation differences, bad-debt reserves, impairment rotation, and interest add-backs for thinly capitalized foreign shareholder loans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The thin capitalization rule limits interest deduction to three times net equity for loans from non-resident controlling shareholders; excess notional interest is added back in Box 5. Interest paid to a non-resident must also comply with withholding and DTA limitation provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base computed as Box 2 less Box 3 less Box 4 plus or minus Box 5 adjustments, reduced by loss carryforward allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation operating through a Korean permanent establishment, Box 6 must reflect profits attributable to the Korean PE on a separate-enterprise basis, excluding head-office general management expenses unless incurred for the benefit of the PE and evidenced by supporting data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Corporate Income Tax Before Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax computation applying the progressive national corporate tax rates to the tax base in Box 6, before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same rate schedule applies to a Korean domestic corporation and to a non-resident corporation with a Korean PE. Foreign dividends and treaty-exempt income must be excluded from the tax base before applying the rate schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Credits, Deductions, and Special Exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development expense credits, SME special deductions, foreign tax credits, employment tax incentives, and corporate restructuring relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Korean PE may claim only those credits granted to a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act or treaty, and must attach the prescribed NTS forms evidencing the credit source and eligibility. Foreign tax credits on remitted profits are limited to foreign tax actually paid and may not exceed Korean corporate tax attributable to the foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Final National Corporate Income Tax After Credits and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net national corporate tax due after subtracting interim prepayments, withheld taxes, and tax credit adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any foreign income tax withheld at source on inbound dividends, interest, or royalties must be reported in this Box and reconciled with the non-resident shareholder's Form 24IR withholding statement. Failure to report cross-border payment flows exposes the entity to the Foreign Transaction Information Report penalty of 20% of the undisclosed amount under Article 47 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of the national corporate income tax in Box 9, payable to the associated local government.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation's Korean permanent establishment is subject to the same 10% local surcharge. No bilateral double taxation avoidance generally reduces the local surcharge, and the amount must be paid separately from the national tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Advance Payments, Withholdings, and Refund Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interim corporate tax prepayments, application of prior-year overpayments, and any refund request due to foreign tax credit excess or carryback.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents using withholding certificates, a refund of over-withholding arising from misapplied DTA rates may be claimed by filing an amended return and Form 'Tax Treaty Refund Application' with the National Tax Service within three years from the filing deadline. Supporting documents must demonstrate beneficial ownership and absence of conduit arrangement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return attracts an unfaithful-return penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax (40% where no return is filed) under Article 47 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus daily delinquency interest calculated at 0.03% per day (roughly 10.95% per annum) from the original due date. Under the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act, fraudulent concealment of revenue may lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to three times the evaded tax; where the tax evaded exceeds KRW 1 billion, the aggravated penalty may exceed 10 years of imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge, producing a combined economic dividend withholding rate of 22%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a bilateral Double Tax Treaty rate on an outbound dividend from a Korean Chusik Hoesa to a non-resident shareholder: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the shareholder's home jurisdiction, (2) execute a Beneficial Ownership Declaration for the dividend recipient, (3) submit the Application for Exemption/Reduction of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaty (Form 24IR) through HomeTax or to the withholding agent before remittance, (4) prove the shareholder maintains economic substance in its residence state and is not a conduit for a third-country resident, and (5) obtain National Tax Service approval or a withholding tax exemption certificate before making the distribution. If the payment is made without authorization, the excess withholding can be claimed by refund within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Korean withholding tax on outbound royalties and interests is 20% national withholding tax plus 10% local surcharge (combined 22%). Under most Korean DTA treaties, the reduced rate for interest is 10% to 15% and for royalties 10% to 15%, subject to the same beneficial ownership and Tax Residency Certificate procedure, and after completion of a non-residents payment registration with the NTS portal.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Article 36 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, a Korean Chusik Hoesa must prepare a Local File and Master File when the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 10 billion per fiscal year; a simplified documentation requirement applies to smaller transactions where the taxpayer has engaged in intercompany transborder dealings with affiliates.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not use the UAE-derived statutory term 'Economic Substance Regulations', but applies a substantive economic-substance doctrine through Article 4 of the Corporate Tax Act, Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, and the place of effective management rules. A foreign shareholder of a Korean Chusik Hoesa must demonstrate that the Korean company executes its core income-generating activities in Korea, maintains director-level substance, keeps board records, has bank accounts, and is not a tax-haven shell. A company incorporated abroad but with effective management in Korea may be recharacterized as a domestic Korean corporation for tax purposes, and treaty benefits can be denied under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule if the shareholder is a mere conduit without local offices, employees, or business operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Concealment of E-commerce Revenue Shell
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating Shopify DTC sales, directing PayPal and Stripe settlement proceeds to a personal account, deleting payment gateway reports, using undisclosed offshore merchant accounts, or recording intercompany payments as fake service expenses to reduce the corporate tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 9 and 11 of the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act impose imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to three times the evaded tax; aggravated punishment is triggered when the tax evaded exceeds KRW 1 billion. The National Tax Service also adds a 20% to 40% understatement or non-filing penalty and daily delinquency surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under Article 42 of the Korean Commercial Act and Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act. A director who knowingly participated in the concealment will be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax with personal asset seizure, international travel ban via NTS blacklisting, civil restitution in shareholder derivative litigation, and criminal imprisonment punishable by the underlying evasion offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Singapore or Hong Kong shelf company with no staff, no office, no independent business activity, no board minutes, and no management decisions outside Korea, solely to channel Korean royalties, dividends, and interest and claim a reduced DTA rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 2-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes denies the treaty rate; Article 92-8 of the International Tax Adjustment Act recharacterizes the intermediary as a Korean shareholder and reattributes intangible income back to Korea. A serious understatement penalty of up to 40% of the recharacterized tax base applies, and prosecution may be referred to the Public Prosecutor's Office for abuse of tax convention.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to veil piercing and become personally liable for the aggregate denied-benefit amount, incur NTS travel blacklisting, be named on the customs turnover report and asset seizure orders, have personal assets traced through foreign accounts, and face criminal imprisonment of up to 10 years in aggravated cases involving artificial conduit arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports for high-risk PayPal, Shopify Payments, or Stripe settlement flows, operating an unlicensed money transmission or virtual asset settlement channel through chargebacks, or deliberately structuring Third-Party Processor deposits to avoid threshold reporting under the Korean financial transaction reporting regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 5 and 6 of the Financial Transaction Reports Act impose imprisonment of up to 5 years or a monetary penalty of up to KRW 100 million for intentional failure to report suspicious transactions; under the Proceeds of Crime Act, any commercial money laundering activity carries forfeiture of assets and imprisonment of up to 14 years for aggravated cases. The Financial Intelligence Unit may also impose administrative fines and revoke the company's foreign exchange banking permissions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court will pierce the corporate veil where a director directed or benefited from the laundering practice, imposing joint liability for launder proceeds, personal asset freezing, travel ban and blacklisting by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit, lifetime disqualification from serving as a director, and criminal imprisonment reflecting the underlying AML offense.
